evidence.quote: In Colorado Revised Statutes, add part 15 to article 21 of title 13 as follows:

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Creates a civil cause of action against persons who disclose or threaten to disclose intimate digital depictions without consent, and amends Colorado criminal and juvenile provisions on such depictions and on sexually exploitative material. Applies to offenses committed on or after the effective date, subject to referendum.
summary.long: New Part 15 (CRS 13-21-1501 to 13-21-1507) gives a depicted individual a civil action against a person who discloses or threatens to disclose an intimate digital depiction without consent, if the person knew or recklessly disregarded that lack of consent, that severe emotional distress would result, and that the individual was identifiable. Consent to disclosure requires a signed, plain-language written agreement with listed contents; disclaimers are no defense. Exceptions cover good-faith reporting, legal proceedings, public-interest matters, satire, technology providers, interactive computer services and broadcasters meeting listed conditions. Remedies include the greater of actual damages or $150,000 liquidated damages, the defendant's monetary gain, exemplary damages, costs and fees, and injunctions. Sections 2 to 8 amend criminal, juvenile and related provisions: disclosure for harassment or pecuniary gain (CRS 18-7-107, 18-7-108) with a court fine of up to $10,000; sexually exploitative material extended to realistic digital depictions of identifiable children (18-6-403); and juvenile offenses (18-7-109). Sections 2 to 8 apply to offenses committed on or after the effective date, subject to a referendum petition.

notes: Sections 2 to 8 and the amended 18-7-107 and 18-7-108 reproduce only changed text, so unchanged subsections are not restated; annotation covers only the quoted changes. Definitions of digital depiction and intimate digital depiction differ across Part 15, 18-7-107, 18-7-108 and 18-7-109 (e.g., Part 15 covers generative AI, while 18-7-109 has no age limit on depicted individuals). The definitions of private intimate parts differ: 18-7-109(8)(n) includes buttocks, while 18-7-107(6)(p) and 18-7-108(6)(p) do not. Section 9(2) applies sections 2 to 8 to offences committed on or after the effective date but does not list section 1 (Part 15). Section 9(1) makes the effective date depend on any referendum petition, with a vote referred to the November 2026 general election. The 2018 deadline in 24-33.5-1803(3)(m) is stated in the text and was not changed by this act. Spot-check (2026-10-14): following the codebook rule for amending acts, thresholds stated only in unchanged (lower-case) restated text (18-7-107/108 actor age 18, 18-7-109 age 14 / four-year gap / 72 hours / image counts, juvenile court age 10) were removed; capitalised text marks the additions. Enforcement rows keep the sanction classes of the amended offenses because their scope now covers intimate digital depictions.

obligations.summary: Creates a civil cause of action against a person who discloses or threatens to disclose an intimate digital depiction without the depicted individual's consent, where the person knew or acted with reckless disregard for the depicted individual's non-consent, severe emotional distress and identifiability. Operates as a civil liability rule rather than an express prohibition.
obligations.applies_from: 12:01 a.m. on the day following the expiration of the ninety-day period after final adjournment of the general assembly
obligations.conditional_on: Subject to the exceptions in 13-21-1504; depicted individual must have suffered harm

obligations.summary: For consent to a disclosure to be valid in an action under 13-21-1503(1), it must be set forth in a written, plain-language agreement signed knowingly and voluntarily, with a general description of the depiction, the agreed specific use (platforms or locations, time period and security features) and, if applicable, the visual work it is incorporated into. Prior consent to creation, or prior consensual disclosure, does not establish consent to later disclosure.

obligations.conditional_on: Applies in an action brought under 13-21-1503(1)

obligations.summary: A broadcaster is protected from liability for third-party content containing an intimate digital depiction only if it did not create or materially contribute to the depiction, lacked actual knowledge that it was non-consensual, and upon obtaining such knowledge acted promptly and in good faith to remove, cease dissemination of, or limit access to it, when reasonably feasible. The protection does not apply if the broadcaster knowingly or recklessly publishes such content or fails to respond to a valid removal request.

obligations.summary: Prohibits a juvenile from knowingly disclosing or threatening to disclose a private intimate image or intimate digital depiction of another individual in listed circumstances (disclosure, possession or exchange of such images, with specified age and consent conditions). Possession is excepted if the juvenile destroys or deletes the image, or reports the initial viewing to law enforcement or a school resource officer, within seventy-two hours. Disclosure is a class 2 misdemeanor with class 1 aggravating cases, possession is a petty offense with a class 2 misdemeanor tier, and exchange is a civil infraction.
